canonical_name: Internet Protocol Version 4 — RFC 791 / STD 5 core

standardized.notes: RFC 791 remains STD 5 / Internet Standard with later updates.

last_known_use.notes: Continues in production networks; current deployment details require implementation/measurement sources.

addressing: 32-bit IPv4 source/destination addressing; historical classful assumptions later transformed by subnetting/VLSM/CIDR without replacing the IPv4 header family.
routing_or_forwarding: Independent datagrams are forwarded toward a destination by hosts/gateways/routers; no virtual-circuit state is required by IPv4 itself.
error_control: IPv4 provides a header checksum but not end-to-end reliability; errors may be reported through ICMP.
flow_or_congestion_control: No end-to-end flow/retransmission mechanism in IPv4 itself.

survival.provenance_notes: Protocol is continuously deployed rather than preserved only as a museum artifact.

open_questions: Track classful addressing assumptions → subnetting/VLSM/CIDR without conflating address architecture with packet format.
Map fragmentation practice and router/host requirement changes.
Preserve packet captures showing directly recognizable RFC 791 header fields.
notes: Reference example for the archive category still-current-original-standard: an early Internet protocol RFC remains part of the current Internet Standards corpus while specific semantics are updated by later documents.
